title: Using LLMs for Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis:The Swedish Nord-syd Case
content: Large language models are increasingly useful as front-end tools for decision support, particularly when extensive textual reports must be read and transformed into a structured analytical form. However, summarisation and decision making are different tasks: summarisation is primarily epistemic compression, whereas choice is normative aggregation. An LLM such as ChatGPT can identify alternatives, criteria, and qualitative assessments in policy documents, but it does not by itself provide a transparent and reproducible method for aggregating conflicting criteria under uncertainty. This paper proposes a hybrid architecture in which ChatGPT prepares the decision basis while a multi-criteria decision analysis tool performs the formal evaluation. The approach is examined through the Swedish Nord-syd infrastructure case. It was first analysed manually in 2011, when human analysts assigned qualitative ratings. In 2025, ChatGPT independently extracted the report-defined alternatives, criteria, and assessments and translated them. The two models were analysed using the same criteria hierarchy, equal local weights, and the same MCDA procedure. The analyses produced closely corresponding aggregate results and the same ranking of alternatives. The study demonstrates that LLMs and MCDA tools are complementary: the former improve access to complex textual evidence, while the latter provide the transparent evaluative structure required for defensible decision support.
